MCP servers

The practical path for connecting CALIBER to MCP servers, verifying discovered tools, and governing remote tool use. Preview: off by default; enable with CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS.

System userDeveloperOperatorHow ToBETA
PrerequisitesA CALIBER deployment with MCP access (CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true)
Reviewed 2026-10-15 · current main branch docs contract

Disabled by default. MCP servers are a preview area and are off by default; enable with CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true and restart CALIBER (the same flag turns on OpenAPI integrations). While it is off, the /mcp-servers* routes answer 404 (reason_code: feature_disabled), the MCP Servers page is hidden, and a workflow MCP node is reported as unavailable ("A registered MCP server that CALIBER can reach (needs CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true)"). Enabling the flag means you accept preview behavior. See Feature flags. The Beta does not change that: GET /capabilities reports adapters.mcp_servers as preview (or unavailable under the reference profile, which lists no MCP command or host) and never supported; see Capability exposure.

Use this page when the practical question is how to connect CALIBER to an MCP server, verify the discovered tools, and govern what remote tools may do.

1. What MCP adds to CALIBER#

MCP lets CALIBER connect to externally hosted tool surfaces without baking each integration directly into the core product. That increases power, but it also raises the need for connection tests, inventories, and policy enforcement.

A server uses one of three transports: stdio, sse or streamable-http. The workflow from the API is POST /mcp-servers, then POST /mcp-servers/{server_id}/test-connection, then POST /mcp-servers/{server_id}/discover-tools, then a per-tool policy with PATCH /mcp-servers/{server_id}/tools/{tool_name}/policy.

A discovered tool is denied until you classify it. Discovery establishes that the tool exists, not that it may run: with no policy a tool is allowed: false. The policy carries allowed, side_effect_level and requires_approval, and an allowed tool whose side_effect_level is write or external_action must set requires_approval (the PATCH answers 400 otherwise). A local stdio server is containment, not isolation; only a managed sidecar or a non-loopback HTTPS endpoint counts as an external execution boundary when a production-class alias is promoted.

A remote server's address is checked against the egress policy as well as the host allowlist, so an endpoint on 127.0.0.1 or a private network address is refused by default ("resolves into the blocked loopback range") even though the allowlist names loopback. Run a server on the CALIBER host over stdio: the command must be on CALIBER_MCP_STDIO_COMMAND_ALLOWLIST, and a Python script must be an allowlisted -m module or an absolute path in CALIBER_MCP_STDIO_PYTHON_SCRIPT_ALLOWLIST. The Governed Tool Connectivity lab runs a real one.

Your policy, not the server's word, decides what a tool may do. A server reports its own tool names, descriptions and hints such as readOnlyHint; CALIBER treats all of it as data and never as a classification. In a workflow, a tool you classified read runs inline; a tool you classified write or external_action is proposed, approved by an exact approval and dispatched once (and left unknown, never resent, if the server's answer is lost, because most MCP servers cannot confirm their own effects); a tool you have not classified, or blocked, is refused with a code such as mcp_tool_unclassified before anything is sent (under the reference profile; the default development profile keeps running a protected tool inline as before, which is not the governed path). The first-party database server's write tools are refused in a workflow under the reference profile. A reference deployment must also set CALIBER_MCP_STDIO_COMMAND_ALLOWLIST and CALIBER_MCP_REMOTE_HOST_ALLOWLIST to empty, so no server is reachable there yet (see MCP allowlists). See Governed MCP tools for the exact codes and recovery.

Inside a project, creating, changing or deleting a server and changing a tool policy need the global caliber.admin scope and editor or owner. Testing the connection, discovering tools and invoking a tool need caliber.admin and reviewer, editor or owner. Saving a tool's test cases needs caliber.operator and editor or owner, and calibrating a tool needs caliber.operator and reviewer or above. A member with too weak a role gets 403 and a person outside the project gets 404.

3. Common failure modes#

SymptomFirst thing to check
There is no MCP Servers page, or a call answers 404 with reason_code: feature_disabledCALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS is off (the default); set it to true and restart
The server connects but tools do not appeardiscovery or transport mismatch
Tools appear but cannot runthe tool has no policy yet (the default is denied), or it needs approval, or its secret-source configuration is wrong
The same tool behaves differently across environmentsendpoint, credentials, or server version drift
